root_cause.text: Using a per-superblock slab cache with a device-specific name (derived from major:minor) for inline xattr entries causes the slab subsystem to merge caches of the same size under one internal name, leading to reference count mismatches upon unmount/remount and a spurious "already exists" warning when re-creating the cache for the same device.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message detail the reproduction: mounting two devices creates two slab caches with different names (e.g., f2fs_xattr_entry-7:3 and f2fs_xattr_entry-7:7) but the same slab size; the slab system merges them into one core structure with the name of the first cache. Destroying the first cache only decrements the reference count, and later re-creating a cache with the same name triggers the WARNING. The patch fixes this by replacing the per-sb cache with a global cache using a fixed name and fixed size (DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE).

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
f2fs: use kmem_cache pool during inline xattr lookups

It's been observed that kzalloc() on lookup_all_xattrs() are call
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit a999150f4fe3abbb7efd05411fd5b460be699943
Author: Chao Yu <chao@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Feb 25 18:17:10 2020 +0800

    f2fs: use kmem_cache pool during inline xattr lookups
    
    It's been observed that kzalloc() on lookup_all_xattrs() are called millions
    of times on Android, quickly becoming the top abuser of slub memory allocator.
    
    Use a dedicated kmem cache pool for xattr lookups to mitigate this.
    
    Signed-off-by: Park Ju Hyung <qkrwngud825@gmail.com>
    Signed-o
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces a per-superblock slab cache with a device-specific name (derived from major:minor) via sprintf(slab_name, "f2fs_xattr_entry-%u:%u", MAJOR(dev), MINOR(dev)) in f2fs_init_xattr_caches. This is exactly the vulnerable pattern described in the root cause: using a per-superblock slab cache with a unique name that can cause slab merging and reference count mismatches upon unmount/remount. The code does not include any mitigation (e.g., using a non-mergeable flag like SLAB_NO_MERGE) to prevent slab merging. Therefore, the vulnerable construct is present and no fix is applied.
